data.narrative:
Orbital Composites is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Cole Nielsen and Amolak Badesha that has raised $6.6M to date. The valuation exercise references a peer set of nine private companies and one public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

A stage-progression method was the only applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($6.6M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for progression from seed to next round, this method yields a midpoint valuation of $16M. This multiplier reflects observed capital efficiency and value creation within the seed-to-Series-A transition window. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied given only one same-stage comparable in the Robotics & Manufacturing universe; expanding to adjacent stages or broader sector peers risked introducing excessive variance.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $14M (low) to $19M (high), with a median point estimate of $16M. This range reflects conservative parametrization of stage-progression mechanics around observed raising patterns. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to sector benchmarks, the timing and terms of the next funding event, and validation of product-market fit within the robotics automation segment. The single-method reliance underscores the importance of gathering additional comparable data as the company moves toward Series A.
